verses.20:9: These were the appointed cities for all the sons of Israel and for the sojourner who resides in their midst, so that anyone who strikes down a person unintentionally might flee there and not die by the hand of the avenger of blood until he stood before the congregation.
verses.21:1: Then the heads of the ancestral houses of the Levites approached Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of the ancestral houses of the tribes of the sons of Israel.
verses.21:2: They spoke to them at Shiloh in the land of Canaan, saying, "The LORD commanded by the hand of Moses to give us cities to live in, and their pasturelands for our livestock."
verses.21:3: So the sons of Israel gave to the Levites from their inheritance, according to the command of the LORD, these cities and their pasturelands.
verses.21:4: The lot came out for the clans of the Kohathites, and to the sons of Aaron the priest, from among the Levites, went thirteen cities by lot from the tribe of Judah, from the tribe of the Simeonites, and from the tribe of Benjamin.
verses.21:5: And to the remaining sons of Kohath went ten cities by lot from the clans of the tribe of Ephraim, from the tribe of Dan, and from the half-tribe of Manasseh.
verses.21:6: And to the sons of Gershon went thirteen cities by lot from the clans of the tribe of Issachar, from the tribe of Asher, from the tribe of Naphtali, and from the half-tribe of Manasseh in Bashan.
verses.21:7: To the sons of Merari, according to their clans, went twelve cities from the tribe of Reuben, from the tribe of Gad, and from the tribe of Zebulun.
verses.21:8: Thus the sons of Israel gave to the Levites these cities and their pasturelands by lot, just as the LORD commanded by the hand of Moses.
verses.21:9: They gave from the tribe of the sons of Judah and from the tribe of the sons of Simeon these cities that are called by name.
verses.21:10: These went to the sons of Aaron, from the clans of the Kohathites, from the sons of Levi, because the lot came to them first.
verses.21:11: They gave them Kiriath-arba, father of Anak—that is, Hebron—in the hill country of Judah, and its pastureland around it.
verses.21:12: Yet they gave the city's fields and its villages to Caleb son of Jephunneh for his possession.
verses.21:13: So to the sons of Aaron the priest they gave the city of refuge for the killer, Hebron, and its pastureland; Libnah and its pastureland;
verses.21:14: Jattir and its pastureland; Eshtemoa and its pastureland;
verses.21:15: Holon and its pastureland; Debir and its pastureland;
verses.21:16: Ain and its pastureland; Juttah and its pastureland; and Beth-shemesh and its pastureland—nine cities from these two tribes.
verses.21:17: And from the tribe of Benjamin: Gibeon and its pastureland; Geba and its pastureland;
verses.21:18: Anathoth and its pastureland; and Almon and its pastureland—four cities.
verses.21:19: All the cities of the sons of Aaron, the priests: thirteen cities and their pasturelands.
verses.21:20: Now as for the clans of the sons of Kohath, the Levites remaining from the sons of Kohath, the cities of their lot came from the tribe of Ephraim.
verses.21:21: They gave them the city of refuge for the killer, Shechem, and its pastureland in the hill country of Ephraim; Gezer and its pastureland;
verses.21:22: Kibzaim and its pastureland; and Beth-horon and its pastureland—four cities.
verses.21:23: And from the tribe of Dan: Elteke and its pastureland; Gibbethon and its pastureland;
verses.21:24: Aijalon and its pastureland; and Gath-rimmon and its pastureland—four cities.
verses.21:25: And from the half-tribe of Manasseh: Taanach and its pastureland; and Gath-rimmon and its pastureland—two cities.
verses.21:26: Ten cities in all, and their pasturelands, belonged to the clans of the remaining sons of Kohath.
verses.21:27: And to the sons of Gershon, from the clans of the Levites, from the half-tribe of Manasseh: the city of refuge for the killer, Golan in Bashan, and its pastureland; and Be-eshterah and its pastureland—two cities.
verses.21:28: And from the tribe of Issachar: Kishion and its pastureland; Daberath and its pastureland;
verses.21:29: Jarmuth and its pastureland; and En-gannim and its pastureland—four cities.
verses.21:30: And from the tribe of Asher: Mishal and its pastureland; Abdon and its pastureland;
verses.21:31: Helkath and its pastureland; and Rehob and its pastureland—four cities.
verses.21:32: And from the tribe of Naphtali: the city of refuge for the killer, Kedesh in Galilee, and its pastureland; Hammoth-dor and its pastureland; and Kartan and its pastureland—three cities.
verses.21:33: All the cities of the Gershonites according to their clans: thirteen cities and their pasturelands.
verses.21:34: And to the clans of the sons of Merari, the remaining Levites, from the tribe of Zebulun: Jokneam and its pastureland; Kartah and its pastureland;
verses.21:35: Dimnah and its pastureland; and Nahalal and its pastureland—four cities.
verses.21:36: ⟦And from the tribe of Reuben: Bezer and its pastureland; Jahaz and its pastureland;⟧
verses.21:37: ⟦Kedemoth and its pastureland; and Mephaath and its pastureland—four cities.⟧
verses.21:38: And from the tribe of Gad: the city of refuge for the killer, Ramoth in Gilead, and its pastureland; Mahanaim and its pastureland;
verses.21:39: Heshbon and its pastureland; and Jazer and its pastureland—four cities in all.
verses.21:40: All the cities for the sons of Merari according to their clans, the ones remaining from the clans of the Levites—their lot was twelve cities.
verses.21:41: All the cities of the Levites within the possession of the sons of Israel: forty-eight cities and their pasturelands.
verses.21:42: These cities were each a city with its pasturelands around it; so it was for all these cities.
verses.21:43: So the LORD gave to Israel the entire land that He had sworn to give to their fathers; they took possession of it and lived in it.
verses.21:44: And the LORD granted them rest all around, according to everything He had sworn to their fathers. Not one man of all their enemies stood before them; all their enemies the LORD gave into their hand.
verses.21:45: Not one word fell short of all the good words that the LORD had spoken to the house of Israel; everything came about.
verses.22:1: Then Joshua summoned the Reubenites, the Gadites, and the half-tribe of Manasseh.
verses.22:2: He said to them, "You have kept everything that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you, and you have heeded my voice in everything I commanded you.
verses.22:3: You have not deserted your brothers during these many days until this day, and you have kept the charge of the command of the LORD your God.
verses.22:4: And now the LORD your God has given rest to your brothers, just as He spoke to them. Therefore now turn and go to your tents, to the land of your possession that Moses the servant of the LORD gave you across the Jordan.
verses.22:5: Only take great care to carry out the command and the law that Moses the servant of the LORD commanded you: to love the LORD your God, to walk in all His ways, to keep His commands, to cling to Him, and to serve Him with all your heart and with all your soul."
verses.22:6: Then Joshua blessed them and sent them off, and they went to their tents.
verses.22:7: Now to one half of the tribe of Manasseh Moses had given land in Bashan, and to its other half Joshua had given land with their brothers across the Jordan to the west. And furthermore, when Joshua sent them off to their tents, he blessed them.
verses.22:8: He spoke to them, saying, "Return to your tents with great wealth and with very much livestock, with silver and gold, with bronze and iron, and with very many garments. Divide the plunder of your enemies with your brothers."
verses.22:9: So the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh turned back and departed from the sons of Israel, from Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan, to go to the land of Gilead, to the land of their possession, of which they had taken possession at the command of the LORD by the hand of Moses.
verses.22:10: When they came to the districts of the Jordan that are in the land of Canaan, the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh built an altar there by the Jordan, an altar great in appearance.
verses.22:11: Then the sons of Israel heard it said, "Look, the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh have built the altar facing the land of Canaan, at the districts of the Jordan, on the side of the sons of Israel."
verses.22:12: When the sons of Israel heard it, the whole congregation of the sons of Israel assembled at Shiloh to go up against them for war.
verses.22:13: Then the sons of Israel sent Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest to the sons of Reuben, to the sons of Gad, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead.
verses.22:14: With him were ten leaders, one leader for each father's house from all the tribes of Israel; each of them was head of his father's house among the thousands of Israel.
verses.22:15: They came to the sons of Reuben, to the sons of Gad, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh in the land of Gilead, and they spoke with them, saying:
verses.22:16: "This is what the whole congregation of the LORD says: 'What is this treachery that you have committed against the God of Israel, turning back today from following the LORD by building an altar for yourselves, to rebel today against the LORD?
verses.22:17: Is the iniquity of Peor too little for us, from which we have not cleansed ourselves until this day, though the plague came upon the congregation of the LORD,
verses.22:18: that you are turning back today from following the LORD? And it will happen that if you rebel today against the LORD, tomorrow He will be angry with the whole congregation of Israel.
verses.22:19: However, if the land of your possession is unclean, cross over to the land of the LORD's possession, where the tabernacle of the LORD dwells, and take possession among us. But do not rebel against the LORD, and do not rebel against us by building an altar for yourselves apart from the altar of the LORD our God.
verses.22:20: Did not Achan son of Zerah commit treachery regarding what was devoted to destruction, and wrath came upon the whole congregation of Israel? And he was not the only man to perish in his iniquity.'"
verses.22:21: Then the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the half-tribe of Manasseh answered and spoke to the heads of the thousands of Israel:
verses.22:22: "God of gods, the LORD! God of gods, the LORD! He knows, and may Israel itself know! If it was in rebellion or in treachery against the LORD—do not save us this day—
verses.22:23: in building an altar for ourselves to turn back from following the LORD, or if it was to offer up burnt offering and grain offering on it, or to present sacrifices of peace offerings on it, may the LORD Himself require it.
verses.22:24: Rather, we truly did this out of anxiety over a matter, thinking that in time to come your sons might say to our sons, 'What do you have to do with the LORD, the God of Israel?
verses.22:25: For the LORD has set the Jordan as a boundary between us and you, you sons of Reuben and sons of Gad; you have no portion in the LORD.' So your sons might make our sons stop fearing the LORD.
verses.22:26: Therefore we said, 'Let us now take action for ourselves to build the altar, not for burnt offering and not for sacrifice,
verses.22:27: rather, it shall be a witness between us and you, and between our generations after us, that we are to perform the service of the LORD before Him with our burnt offerings, with our sacrifices, and with our peace offerings,' so that your sons will not say in time to come to our sons, 'You have no portion in the LORD.'
verses.22:28: And we thought that if it should happen that they speak to us or to our generations in time to come, then we would say, 'Look at the replica of the altar of the LORD that our fathers made, not for burnt offering and not for sacrifice; rather, it is a witness between us and you.'
verses.22:29: Far be it from us indeed to rebel against the LORD and to turn back today from following the LORD by building an altar for burnt offering, for grain offering, and for sacrifice, besides the altar of the LORD our God that is before His tabernacle."
verses.22:30: When Phinehas the priest, the leaders of the congregation, and the heads of the thousands of Israel who were with him heard the words that the sons of Reuben, the sons of Gad, and the sons of Manasseh spoke, it was good in their sight.
verses.22:31: Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest said to the sons of Reuben, to the sons of Gad, and to the sons of Manasseh, "Today we know that the LORD is in our midst, because you have not committed this treachery against the LORD. Now you have delivered the sons of Israel from the hand of the LORD."
verses.22:32: Then Phinehas son of Eleazar the priest and the leaders returned from the sons of Reuben and from the sons of Gad, from the land of Gilead to the land of Canaan, to the sons of Israel, and brought back word to them.
verses.22:33: The report was good in the sight of the sons of Israel, and the sons of Israel blessed God and did not speak of going up against them for war to destroy the land in which the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad were living.
verses.22:34: And the sons of Reuben and the sons of Gad named the altar, "It is a witness between us that the LORD is God."
verses.23:1: Now it came about, many days after the LORD had given rest to Israel from all their enemies on every side, that Joshua was old, advanced in days.
verses.23:2: So Joshua summoned all Israel, its elders, its heads, its judges, and its officers, and said to them, "I have grown old; I am advanced in days.
verses.23:3: And you yourselves have seen everything that the LORD your God has done to all these nations on your account, for the LORD your God, He is the One who fights for you.
verses.23:4: Look, I have allotted to you these remaining nations as an inheritance for your tribes, from the Jordan—along with all the nations that I have cut off—to the Great Sea toward the setting of the sun.
verses.23:5: And the LORD your God Himself will thrust them back before you and drive them out from before you, and you will take possession of their land, just as the LORD your God spoke to you.
verses.23:6: Therefore be very strong to keep and to carry out everything written in the book of the law of Moses, not turning aside from it to the right or to the left,
verses.23:7: so that you do not mingle with these nations, these that remain with you; and you shall not mention the name of their gods, nor make anyone swear by them, nor serve them, nor bow down to them.
verses.23:8: Rather, you shall cling to the LORD your God, just as you have done until this day.
verses.23:9: For the LORD has driven out great and mighty nations from before you; and as for you, no man has stood before you until this day.
verses.23:10: One man from among you chases a thousand, for the LORD your God, He is the One who fights for you, just as He spoke to you.
verses.23:11: Therefore watch closely over your souls, to love the LORD your God.
verses.23:12: For if you ever turn back and cling to the remnant of these nations, these that remain with you, and intermarry with them, and mingle with them and they with you,
verses.23:13: know for certain that the LORD your God will not continue to drive out these nations from before you; and they will become a snare and a trap for you, and a whip on your sides, and thorns in your eyes, until you perish from this good land that the LORD your God has given you.
verses.23:14: Now look, today I am going the way of all the earth, and you know with your whole heart and with your whole soul that not a single word has fallen short of all the good words that the LORD your God spoke concerning you. All of it has come about for you; not a single word of it has fallen short.
verses.23:15: And it will happen that just as every good thing that the LORD your God spoke to you has come upon you, so the LORD will bring upon you every harmful thing, until He has destroyed you from this good land that the LORD your God has given you.
verses.23:16: When you transgress the covenant of the LORD your God, which He commanded you, and go and serve other gods and bow down to them, then the anger of the LORD will burn against you, and you will perish quickly from the good land that He has given you."
verses.24:1: Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel to Shechem, and he summoned the elders of Israel, its heads, its judges, and its officers; and they took their stand before God.
verses.24:2: And Joshua said to all the people, "This is what the LORD, the God of Israel, says: 'Beyond the River your fathers lived from ancient times—Terah, the father of Abraham and the father of Nahor—and they served other gods.
verses.24:3: And I took your father Abraham from beyond the River, and I led him throughout the entire land of Canaan, multiplied his offspring, and gave him Isaac.
verses.24:4: And I gave Jacob and Esau to Isaac. I gave Mount Seir to Esau to take possession of it, while Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt.
verses.24:5: And I sent Moses and Aaron, and I struck Egypt with what I did in its midst; and after that I brought you out.
verses.24:6: So I brought your fathers out from Egypt, and you came to the sea, and the Egyptians pursued after your fathers with chariots and with horsemen to the Red Sea.
verses.24:7: And they cried out to the LORD, and He set deep darkness between you and the Egyptians, and He brought the sea over them and covered them. Your eyes saw what I did in Egypt, and you lived in the wilderness many days.
verses.24:8: And I brought you into the land of the Amorites who were living beyond the Jordan, and they fought against you. I gave them into your hand, and you took possession of their land, and I destroyed them from before you.
verses.24:9: And Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab, rose up and fought against Israel; he sent and called for Balaam son of Beor to curse you.
verses.24:10: Yet I was not willing to listen to Balaam; so he indeed blessed you, and I rescued you from his hand.
verses.24:11: And you crossed over the Jordan and came to Jericho, and the citizens of Jericho fought against you, the Amorites, the Perizzites, the Canaanites, the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Hivites, and the Jebusites; and I gave them into your hand.
verses.24:12: And I sent the hornet ahead of you, and it drove them out from before you, the two kings of the Amorites—not by your sword and not by your bow.
verses.24:13: And I gave you a land on which you did not toil and cities that you did not build, and you live in them; you are eating from vineyards and olive groves that you did not plant.'
verses.24:14: So now, fear the LORD and serve Him in integrity and in truth, and remove the gods that your fathers served beyond the River and in Egypt, and serve the LORD.
verses.24:15: And if it is evil in your sight to serve the LORD, today choose for yourselves whom you will serve—whether the gods that your fathers served, those from beyond the River, or the gods of the Amorites in whose land you live. But I and my house—we will serve the LORD."
verses.24:16: And the people answered and said, "Far be it from us to abandon the LORD to serve other gods,
verses.24:17: for the LORD our God, He is the One who brought us and our fathers up from the land of Egypt, from the house of slaves, and who did these great signs before our eyes, and guarded us along the entire way in which we walked and among all the peoples whose midst we passed through.
verses.24:18: And the LORD drove out all the peoples and the Amorites living in the land from before us. We too will serve the LORD, for He is our God."
verses.24:19: And Joshua said to the people, "You cannot serve the LORD, because He is a holy God; He is a jealous God. He will not forgive your rebellion or your sins.
verses.24:20: If you abandon the LORD and serve foreign gods, He will turn and do harm to you and bring you to an end, after He has done good for you."
verses.24:21: And the people said to Joshua, "No, rather we will serve the LORD."
verses.24:22: Then Joshua said to the people, "You are witnesses against yourselves that it is you who have chosen for yourselves the LORD, to serve Him." And they said, "We are witnesses."
verses.24:23: "So now, remove the foreign gods that are in your midst, and incline your heart toward the LORD, the God of Israel."
verses.24:24: And the people said to Joshua, "It is the LORD our God we will serve, and His voice we will heed."
verses.24:25: And Joshua made a covenant with the people on that day, and he set a statute and an ordinance for them at Shechem.
verses.24:26: Joshua wrote these words in the book of the law of God; then he took a great stone and erected it there beneath the oak that was in the sanctuary of the LORD.
verses.24:27: And Joshua said to all the people, "Look, this stone will be a witness against us, because it has heard all the words of the LORD that He spoke with us; and it will be a witness against you, so that you do not deal falsely with your God."
verses.24:28: Then Joshua sent the people away, each man to his inheritance.
verses.24:29: And Israel served the LORD all the days of Joshua and all the days of the elders who lived on after Joshua, and who had known all the work of the LORD that He had done for Israel.
verses.24:30: And it happened after these things that Joshua son of Nun, the servant of the LORD, died at one hundred and ten years of age.
verses.24:31: They buried him within the territory of his inheritance at Timnath-serah, which is in the hill country of Ephraim, to the north of Mount Gaash.
verses.24:32: And the bones of Joseph, which the sons of Israel had brought up out of Egypt, they buried at Shechem, in the plot of the field that Jacob had purchased from the sons of Hamor, the father of Shechem, for one hundred pieces of money; and it became an inheritance for the sons of Joseph.
verses.24:33: Now Eleazar son of Aaron died, and they buried him at Gibeah of his son Phinehas, which had been given to him in the hill country of Ephraim.

notes.1:7: The Hiphil verb תַּשְׂכִּיל (from שׂכל) combines prudent conduct with resulting success (paired with Hiphil תַּצְלִיחַ in 1:8). Also, מִמֶּנּוּ ("from it") is masculine singular, referring ad sensum to the feminine noun הַתּוֹרָה ("the law") as a body of instruction or book.
notes.1:8: Hebrew דְּרָכֶךָ ("your ways") is vocalized as a plural stem written defectively without the yod (-ֶךָ for -ֶיךָ), rather than singular דַּרְכֶּךָ.
notes.1:14: Hebrew חֲמֻשִׁים ("armed") is a Qal passive participle of debated etymology (either equipped for combat or arrayed in battle divisions), describing warriors ready for battle.
notes.2:4: The Masoretic Text reads וַתִּצְפְּנוֹ (literally "and hid him"), using a masculine singular object suffix commonly understood distributively as "hid each of them."
notes.2:13: Ketiv אחותי could be read as singular ("my sister") or a defective plural; the translated Qere אַחְיוֹתַי explicitly specifies the plural "my sisters."
notes.2:17: The Masoretic Text pairs the feminine noun שְׁבוּעָה ("oath") with the masculine demonstrative הַזֶּה ("this"), a grammatical gender incongruence preserved in the text.
notes.2:18: Hebrew תִּקְוָה here denotes a "cord" or "line" (from a root meaning to twist or bind, homonymous with תִּקְוָה, "hope"), reinforced by חוּט ("thread").
notes.3:4: Hebrew מִתְּמוֹל שִׁלְשׁוֹם ("previously") is a standard idiom literally meaning "from yesterday and the day before yesterday."
notes.3:11: The Masoretic Text places the definite article on הַבְּרִית within the chain אֲרוֹן הַבְּרִית אֲדוֹן כׇּל־הָאָרֶץ, treating "ark of the covenant" as a fixed compound governing "the Lord of all the earth" (similar to definite הָאָרוֹן in construct position in 3:14 and 3:17).
notes.3:16: Ketiv reads באדם ("at/in Adam"), while the translated Qere reads מֵאָדָם ("from Adam"), marking the upstream point from which the dammed waters rose. Also, תַּמּוּ נִכְרָתוּ pairs Qal תָּמַם ("finished") with Niphal כָּרַת ("were cut off") in verbal hendiadys ("were completely cut off").
notes.4:3: The word translated "firmly" is the Hiphil infinitive absolute of kun (spelled plene as hakin), used adverbially to describe the steady stance of the priests' feet.
notes.4:18: Ketiv reads "upon the going up" (b-alot), while the Qere followed here reads "as soon as [they] came up" (k-alot).
notes.4:21: The relative particle asher introduces a temporal clause ("when"), and mahar (literally "tomorrow") is used idiomatically for "in time to come."
notes.4:24: The Hebrew uses a proleptic object construction ("know the hand of the LORD, that it is mighty") and pairs lemaan ("so that") with the Qal perfect yeratem ("you may fear").
notes.5:1: Ketiv reads first-person plural "until we had crossed over" (abrenu), while the Qere followed here reads third-person plural "until they had crossed over" (abram).
notes.5:3: Literally "the Hill of the Foreskins" (Hebrew Gibeath-haaraloth).
notes.5:9: The place name Gilgal plays on the verb galloti ("I have rolled away," Qal perfect of galal).
notes.5:15: Both "sandal" and "foot" are singular in the Masoretic Hebrew, contrasting with the plural forms in Exodus 3:5.
notes.6:1: "Closed and tightly shut up" renders the paired Qal active participle and Pual passive participle of sagar ("shut"), emphasizing total enclosure.
notes.6:7: Ketiv reads plural "and they said" (wayyomeru), while the Qere followed here reads singular "and he said" (wayyomer), referring to Joshua.
notes.6:9: Ketiv reads the Qal perfect "they blew" (taqeu), while the Qere followed here reads the Qal active participle construct "who were blowing" (toqee).
notes.6:13: Ketiv reads the Qal active participle (holek), while the Qere followed here reads the Qal infinitive absolute (halok), matching the paired infinitive absolute wetaqoa ("going on and blowing").
notes.6:18: The Masoretic Hebrew reads taharimu, Hiphil imperfect of haram ("devote to destruction"), understood here reflexively as "devote yourselves to destruction" rather than emending to the Septuagint's "covet."
notes.6:26: The verb wayyashba is Hiphil of shaba ("imposed an oath"), and the preposition b- on "his firstborn" and "his youngest" is the beth of price ("at the price of").
notes.7:1: The Hebrew noun cherem denotes persons or property irrevocably dedicated to the LORD for destruction; taking from it brought Israel itself under the same status in 7:12.
notes.7:5: Hebrew ha-Shebarim carries the definite article and may denote either a proper place name, Shebarim, or a topographic feature meaning the quarries or the clefts.
notes.7:17: Unlike the Niphal passive vayyilaked in 7:16, 7:17b, and 7:18, the verb here is Qal active vayyilkod with an object marker, referring to Joshua taking the clan by lot or functioning impersonally. Hebrew also uses the singular mishpachat collectively for the clans of Judah.
notes.7:21: Ketiv reads the unapocopated Qal wayyiqtol va-er'eh, while Qere reads the standard apocopated form va-ere; both mean I saw. Hebrew leshon literally means tongue, denoting a tongue-shaped bar or ingot of gold.
notes.7:25: Joshua plays on the root akar, meaning to bring trouble on, foreshadowing the place name Valley of Achor in 7:26. The Masoretic text uses two distinct verbs for stoning, ragam with singular him and saqal with plural them after burning.
notes.8:14: Hebrew la-mo'ed can mean either at the appointed place or at the appointed time; followed by facing the Arabah, it likely designates a prearranged battle position.
notes.8:15: The verb vayyinnage'u is the sole Niphal occurrence of naga in the Hebrew Bible, used here in a tolerative sense meaning allowed themselves to be struck or beaten.
notes.8:16: Ketiv reads ba-ir, in the city, while Qere reads ba-Ai, in Ai; this translation follows the Qere.
notes.8:20: Hebrew lo hayah bahem yadayim literally reads there were no hands in them, an idiom for having no power or room to escape.
notes.9:2: "With one voice" literally renders "one mouth" (peh echad).
notes.9:4: The verb rendered "posed as envoys" is the Hithpael wayyiqtol of tsyr (wayyitstayyaru), related to tsir ("envoy, messenger"), contrasting with the similar-looking Hithpael of tsyd ("packed as provisions") in 9:12.
notes.9:7: The written ketiv reads plural "they said" (wy'mrw), whereas the read qere followed here has singular "said" (wayyomer) agreeing grammatically with the collective singular "man of Israel" (ish-yisrael); the verse also has a minor orthographic ketiv/qere on "make" ('krwt / ekhrat-), and the direct speech uses collective first-person singular pronouns in Hebrew.
notes.9:20: The clause "we will let them live" translates a Hiphil infinitive absolute of chayah (hachayeh) continuing the finite verb "we will do," a classical Hebrew construction for coordinated future or modal action.
notes.10:10: The subsequent 3ms verbs ("struck... pursued... struck") have no newly stated subject in Hebrew, leaving open whether the LORD or Israel/Joshua is the grammatical subject.
notes.10:12: The imperative "be still" translates the Qal imperative of damam (dom, "be still, cease, halt"), paired in 10:13 with amad ("stood"); "the Book of Jashar" (10:13) literally means "the Book of the Upright."
notes.10:14: In both 10:14 and 10:42, the verb "was fighting" (nilcham) is pointed as a Niphal participle, highlighting continuous divine action; verses 10:15 and 10:43 of the standard Masoretic Text are absent from this critical Hebrew text, matching the Septuagint.
notes.10:19: The verb rendered "attack them from the rear" is the Piel of zanav (denominative from zanav, "tail"), meaning to strike the rear guard or cut off stragglers.
notes.10:21: The idiom "sharpened his tongue" (charats ... et-leshono, cf. Exodus 11:7) means that no one dared utter a hostile word against any Israelite.
notes.11:2: Hebrew naphoth dor (feminine plural construct of naphah, 'height' or 'upland') denotes the elevated coastal territory around Dor, sometimes transliterated Naphoth-dor; compare the singular construct in 12:23.
notes.11:11: Hebrew hacharem is the Hiphil infinitive absolute of charam, used adverbially to express the solemn ban of devoting persons or cities to complete destruction; it is distinct from the Hiphil of shamad ('destroy') in 11:14 and 11:20.
notes.11:13: Literally 'on their mound' (singular tel with a plural suffix used distributively), referring to fortified cities built atop tells, the artificial hills formed by accumulated layers of earlier settlements.
notes.11:20: Hebrew lechazzeq is the Piel infinitive construct of chazaq (literally 'to strengthen' or 'to make firm,' idiomatically 'to harden'); the conjunction ki following the negative clause lebhilti functions adversatively ('but rather').
notes.12:1: Hebrew mizrachah hashemesh attaches the directional ending -ah directly to the construct noun mizrach ('rising') before 'the sun,' an uncommon construction denoting eastward direction.
notes.12:4: The Masoretic Text literally reads 'and the border/territory of Og' (ugevul Og), even though the following masculine singular participles ('who lived' and 'ruling' in 12:5) describe Og himself.
notes.12:18: The Masoretic pointing lasharon consists of the preposition le-, the definite article, and Sharon ('belonging to the Sharon'), though it is traditionally rendered as the place name Lasharon since the list counts him among the thirty-one kings.
notes.12:23: Hebrew goyim literally means 'nations' and is here treated as the proper name Goiim; the Masoretic Text reads 'in Gilgal' (legilgal), and 'in the upland of Dor' uses the singular construct naphath (compare plural naphoth in 11:2).
notes.13:4: The Masoretic verse division places "from the south" (mitteman) at the start of v. 4 with "all the land of the Canaanites," though some interpreters connect it to the Avvim at the end of v. 3.
notes.13:6: "Allot it" renders a Hiphil imperative of napal ("cause to fall"), an idiom for assigning territory by the casting of lots.
notes.13:8: "With him" (Hebrew immo) refers to the eastern half of the tribe of Manasseh, in contrast to the half-tribe mentioned at the end of v. 7.
notes.13:14: In the first clause "he" refers to Moses, whereas in the final clause "He" refers to the LORD. Although "the fire offerings" is plural, the Hebrew resumptive pronoun hu is masculine singular, serving as the copula.
notes.13:26: "Of Debir" follows the Masoretic vocalization of lidbir as the preposition le- plus the place name Debir; alternatively, the consonants are sometimes read as a single Transjordanian place name, Lidebir (cf. Lo-debar in 2 Sam 9:4).
notes.14:1: Hebrew contrasts two stems of the verb nahal: the Qal ("inherited") for Israel's reception of the land and the Piel ("assigned") for the leaders' distribution of it as an inheritance. "Heads of the ancestral houses" renders the idiomatic shorthand "heads of the fathers."
notes.14:8: "Caused ... to melt" translates the rare Aramaizing Hiphil form himsiw (from masas/masa). "Completely followed" renders the Piel idiom mille ahare, literally "filled after" (also in vv. 9, 14).
notes.14:12: "With me" renders oti, here a Masoretic orthographic variant of the preposition itti ("with me") rather than the direct object marker.
notes.14:15: "He" (hu) refers to Arba, the namesake of Kiriath-arba ("City of Arba"). The definite adjective with be- ("the great man among the Anakim") expresses the Hebrew superlative ("the greatest man among the Anakim").
notes.15:4: The Qere reads plural 'were' (agreeing with plural 'endpoints', as in verses 7 and 11), whereas the Ketiv has singular 'was'. The Hebrew also shifts unexpectedly to second-person plural ('your') at the close of the verse, echoing the border formula in Numbers 34.
notes.15:12: Literally 'the Great Sea and border', an established Hebrew geographical phrase (cf. Numbers 34:6) referring to the Mediterranean Sea together with its shoreline as the western boundary.
notes.15:18: The rare Qal verb translated 'dismounted' occurs only here, in the parallel account in Judges 1:14, and in Judges 4:21 (of a tent peg sinking into the ground); with 'from upon the donkey' it is traditionally understood as sliding down or dismounting.
notes.15:32: The Masoretic summary gives a total of twenty-nine cities, whereas thirty-six city names appear in verses 21-32 (treating Hazor-hadattah and Kerioth-hezron as compound names). Similar numerical discrepancies occur in other town lists in Joshua, possibly reflecting later administrative additions or towns subsequently allotted to Simeon.
notes.15:45: Hebrew literally reads 'its daughters', a geographical idiom for surrounding satellite towns dependent on a major city, as distinct from unwalled 'villages' (also in verse 47).
notes.15:47: The Qere reads 'the Great' ('the Great Sea and its coastline', matching verse 12), whereas the Ketiv reads 'the border', likely an accidental anticipation of the following word.
notes.15:53: The Qere reads the place name 'Janum', whereas the Ketiv reads 'Janim'.
notes.15:63: The Qere reads the Qal perfect of the verb 'be able', whereas the Ketiv reads the Qal imperfect form; with the negation both convey 'were unable' in this past-tense clause.
notes.16:1: The phrase "into the wilderness, ascending" renders the abrupt Hebrew construction "the wilderness, going up" (masculine singular Qal participle), taking "the wilderness" as an adverbial accusative of direction for the boundary.
notes.16:9: The phrase "set apart" translates a rare feminine plural noun derived from the root "to separate," standing in apposition to "the cities."
notes.16:10: The phrase "forced labor" translates a Hebrew expression literally meaning "a serving levy" (corvee labor).
notes.17:4: "According to the command of the LORD" literally reads "to the mouth of the LORD," an idiom for divine command. The verb "he gave" is masculine singular in the Hebrew text, referring to Joshua.
notes.17:11: Here and in verse 16, "its surrounding towns" literally reads "its daughters," the Hebrew idiom for dependent towns around a main city. "The three heights" translates a difficult Hebrew phrase literally meaning "three of the height/region," referring to three upland districts (sometimes rendered "the third is Napheth").
notes.17:14: "Since the LORD has blessed me thus far" renders a stacked Hebrew idiom literally meaning "to the extent that up to here the LORD has blessed me."
notes.17:15: The verb "clear" (here and in verse 18) is the Piel stem of a root meaning "to cut down" or "clear forest," distinct from the Qal verb "to create."
notes.17:18: The Hebrew conjunction "ki" appears five times in this verse with shifting adversative ("but"), concessive ("though" / "even though"), and causal ("for") senses.
notes.18:4: "Record it in writing" (here and in verses 6, 8, and 9) renders the Hebrew verb "to write" with the land as its direct object, meaning to survey and document the territory.
notes.18:12: Here and in verses 14 and 19, the written text (Ketiv) has the singular verb "was," while the read text (Qere) has the plural "were" to agree with the plural subject "outer limits." In verses 12, 13, 16, 18, and 19, "slope" literally renders "shoulder."
notes.18:15: The Masoretic Hebrew text reads "westward," though the overall southern line runs eastward from Kiriath-jearim toward Nephtoah and Jerusalem, perhaps reflecting a brief westward bend or a difficult geographic reading.
notes.18:19: In addition to the plural verb Qere (see note on verse 12), the written text (Ketiv) reads "its outer limits," while the read text (Qere) reads the construct form "the outer limits of the boundary." The word "bay" literally reads "tongue."
notes.18:24: Following the read text (Qere), this name is rendered "Chephar-ammonah"; the written text (Ketiv) reads "Chephar-ammoni."
notes.18:28: In the Masoretic text, "Gibeath" and "Kiriath" stand as separate names, bringing the list in verses 25-28 to the stated total of fourteen cities.
notes.19:2: The Masoretic Text reads 'Beersheba and Sheba,' yielding fourteen town names before the thirteen-city total in v. 6; the conjunction may be epexegetical ('that is, Sheba') or reflect a double name.
notes.19:13: The Pual participle translated 'curving' (from a root meaning 'to trace or mark out' a boundary, cf. Josh 15:9; 18:14) describes the border bending toward Neah, though some take it as part of a compound name Rimmon-methoar.
notes.19:22: Ketiv writes Shahazumah; qere reads Shahazimah.
notes.19:29: Ketiv writes a prefix-conjugation form with waw, while qere reads the weqatal form ('and ... were') matching the surrounding boundary verbs and vv. 14 and 22. The phrase 'from the region of Achzib' translates the Masoretic wording directly.
notes.19:34: The Masoretic Text includes 'and Judah' at the Jordan on the east, even though Judah lay far to the south; some connect this to Judean-affiliated clans in Transjordan (cf. 1 Chr 2:21-22), while the Septuagint omits 'Judah.'
notes.20:3: The Hebrew term translated 'killer' (Qal active participle of the verb for killing) covers both intentional and accidental homicide, and is here qualified as unintentional and without knowledge.
notes.20:7: The verb 'consecrated' renders the Hiphil of the root for holiness, marking the cities of refuge as set apart for sacred asylum, in contrast to 'designated' (Qal of 'give') in vv. 2 and 8.
notes.20:8: Ketiv writes Golon/Galon; qere reads Golan.
notes.20:9: 'Appointed' renders a unique biblical feminine form derived from the verb 'to appoint,' denoting officially designated cities of refuge.
notes.21:9: The Hebrew uses an impersonal third-person masculine singular Qal imperfect (yiqra, literally 'which one calls by name') with a feminine plural direct object referring to the cities, rendered passively in English.
notes.21:25: The Masoretic Text reads 'Gath-rimmon' here (the same name as the Danite city in v. 24), whereas the parallel list in 1 Chronicles 6:70 (MT 6:55) reads Bileam (Ibleam).
notes.21:27: Following the Qere (read form), 'Golan' is translated here; the Ketiv (written form) transposes the two medial consonants (glwn, i.e., Golon or Galon).
notes.21:36: Verses 36-37 are bracketed because they are absent from major early Masoretic codices such as the Leningrad and Aleppo manuscripts (likely due to scribal omission), though they appear in other Hebrew manuscripts and the Septuagint and are required by the totals in vv. 7, 40, and 41 (cf. 1 Chr 6:78-79).
notes.21:45: Literally 'not a word fell from all the good word that the LORD spoke,' combining the idiom of a word 'falling' (failing) with a threefold repetition of the Hebrew root for 'word/speak' (d-b-r).
notes.22:7: The ketiv reads מעבר ('from across'), while the qere followed here reads בְּעֵבֶר ('across / on the side of'), specifying the western side of the Jordan.
notes.22:14: Hebrew אַלְפֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל (literally 'thousands of Israel') refers to traditional tribal military subdivisions or clans.
notes.22:19: Hebrew וְאֹתָנוּ אַל־תִּמְרֹדוּ uses the Qal verb מָרַד ('rebel') with the direct-object pronoun אֹתָנוּ ('us'), meaning 'do not rebel against us,' parallel to 'do not rebel against the LORD.'
notes.22:22: The solemn invocation אֵל אֱלֹהִים יְהוָה may be construed as a construct chain ('God of gods, the LORD') or as three appositional titles ('The Mighty One, God, the LORD'). The parenthetical Hiphil jussive אַל־תּוֹשִׁיעֵנוּ ('do not save us') briefly addresses God directly in the second person.
notes.22:34: The Masoretic Text has no separate name word before recitative כִּי, so the clause itself functions as the altar's name; some later Hebrew manuscripts and the Syriac supply עֵד ('Witness').
notes.23:4: Hebrew הִפַּלְתִּי (Hiphil of נָפַל, literally 'I have caused to fall') is an idiom for apportioning territory by lot. The geographic span מִן־הַיַּרְדֵּן ... וְהַיָּם הַגָּדוֹל omits a second preposition ('to') before 'the Great Sea.'
notes.23:7: Hebrew תַשְׁבִּיעוּ is Hiphil of שָׁבַע ('cause to swear / put under oath'), rather than Niphal ('swear'), forbidding Israelites from imposing oaths in the name of foreign gods.
notes.23:13: Hebrew שֹׁטֵט ('whip / scourge') is a hapax legomenon related to שׁוֹט ('whip'), varying the parallel imagery of Numbers 33:55.
notes.24:3: Ketiv writes a shortened consonantal form lacking the final he, while qere supplies the full Hiphil wayyiqtol 1st-person singular form of rabah ("and I multiplied"), translated here.
notes.24:7: The Masoretic Hebrew shifts within the LORD's speech from first person to third person ("He set ... He brought ... covered") and back to first person ("what I did"), using singular collective suffixes ("over them ... covered them") referring to Egypt.
notes.24:8: Ketiv reads a form with a final paragogic he and without yod, while qere reads the standard Hiphil wayyiqtol 1st-person singular of bo ("and I brought"), which fits the direct object ("you") and is translated here.
notes.24:15: Ketiv reads the preposition be-ever ("beyond"), matching vv. 2 and 14, whereas qere reads me-ever ("from beyond" or "on the other side of"), translated here.
notes.24:19: Hebrew pairs the plural adjective qedoshim ("holy") with the plural noun elohim ("God") as a plural of majesty, while the singular pronoun hu ("He") and singular el-qanno ("a jealous God") confirm singular reference to the LORD.
